title: Multinomial Entropy Formalization
description: Formalizes the Shannon entropy H(X) = -∑ P(k) log P(k) of the multinomial distribution, proving non-negativity and zero-trial determinism

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib
meta.assumptions: Axiom-free: all theorems fully proved with no axiom declarations and no structure-encoded assumptions. Proved: multinomialEntropy_nonneg, multinomialEntropy_zero_trials, multinomialProb_n1_indicator, multinomialEntropy_n1_eq_source, multinomialEntropy_upper_bound, multinomialEntropy_binomial.
originalContributions: multinomialEntropy: Shannon entropy definition for multinomial distribution
multinomialEntropy_nonneg: H(X) ≥ 0 for valid probability vectors (proved)
multinomialEntropy_upper_bound: H(X) ≤ log|Comp(s,n)| via Gibbs inequality (proved)

overview.historicalContext: Shannon entropy $H(X) = -\sum_x P(X=x)\log P(X=x)$ was introduced by Claude Shannon in 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication' (1948) as the fundamental measure of information in a discrete probability distribution. For the multinomial distribution — which models the frequencies of $k$ categories in $n$ independent trials — the entropy captures the uncertainty in the composition of outcomes. Boltzmann had earlier used a related quantity in statistical mechanics, and the connection to combinatorics (the log of the multinomial coefficient) was noted by Boltzmann, Planck, and Einstein. For the multinomial, $H(X) = -\sum_{k: \sum k_i = n} \binom{n}{k_1,\ldots,k_r} \prod p_i^{k_i} \cdot \log\left(\binom{n}{k_1,\ldots,k_r} \prod p_i^{k_i}\right)$, which does not simplify to a closed form in general but achieves its maximum $H = \log\binom{n+r-1}{r-1}$ for the uniform distribution $p_i = 1/r$.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (OQ-02 from binomial-theorem-oq-02-oq-01-oq-01)**: Can the entropy $H(X) = -\sum_k P(X=k) \log P(X=k)$ of the multinomial distribution be formalized in Lean 4?

**Answer**: Yes. We construct `multinomialEntropy s p n : ℝ` as a finite sum over the compositions `s.piAntidiag n`, using `multinomialProb s p n k` from the parent file as the probability mass function. The formalization requires: (1) handling the $0 \cdot \log 0 = 0$ convention (automatic via `Real.log 0 = 0`), (2) non-negativity via `Finset.single_le_sum` and normalization, and (3) connecting to the source entropy $H(p)$ at $n=1$.
overview.text: Shannon entropy of the multinomial distribution is formalizable in Lean 4, with non-negativity provable from the normalization theorem already in the parent file
overview.proofStrategy: Define entropy as a finite sum over piAntidiag, prove non-negativity using single_le_sum + multinomialProb_sum_eq_one, prove structural results using bijection between piAntidiag s 1 and s.
keyInsights: The non-negativity of entropy follows from two facts already proved in the parent file: multinomialProb_nonneg (P(k) ≥ 0) and multinomialProb_sum_eq_one (∑ P(k) = 1 implies P(k) ≤ 1). These together give P(k) ∈ [0,1], and -P·log P ≥ 0 for such values.

The 0·log(0) = 0 convention is automatic in Lean/Mathlib since Real.log 0 = 0, so 0 * Real.log 0 = 0 without any special-casing — the `if prob = 0 then 0 else ...` guard is a belt-and-suspenders precaution for clean splitting.

At n=1, the multinomial distribution IS the source distribution: P(X = indicator_j) = p_j for each j ∈ s, so H(Multinomial(1,p)) = -∑ pᵢ log pᵢ. This is the fundamental connection between the entropy of a single trial and the entropy of the source.
At n=0, there is exactly one outcome (the all-zeros composition with probability 1), giving H = 0. This confirms: zero trials means complete certainty.
The upper bound H(X) ≤ log|Comp(s,n)| holds by the Gibbs inequality applied to the uniform distribution on Comp(s,n). The number of compositions |Comp(s,n)| = C(n+|s|-1, |s|-1) by stars-and-bars.
prerequisites: Shannon entropy and information theory basics

sections.title: Multinomial Entropy Definition
sections.summary: Defines multinomialEntropy as -∑_{k ∈ piAntidiag} (if P(k)=0 then 0 else P(k)·log P(k))
sections.mathContext: The Shannon entropy $H(X) = -\sum_{k \in \text{Comp}(s,n)} P(X=k) \log P(X=k)$ with convention $0 \cdot \log 0 = 0$.

sections.title: Non-negativity (Fully Proved)
sections.summary: Proves H(X) ≥ 0: each term -P·log P ≥ 0 because P ∈ [0,1] and log is nonpositive there.
sections.mathContext: $P(k) \in [0,1]$ follows from non-negativity (multinomialProb_nonneg) and normalization via Finset.single_le_sum. Then $-P \log P \geq 0$ by Real.log_nonpos.

sections.title: Zero Entropy at n=0
sections.summary: Proves H(Multinomial(0,p)) = 0: unique composition all-zero with probability 1.

sections.title: Source Entropy Recovery at n=1
sections.summary: multinomialProb_n1_indicator (proved): P(δ_j) = p_j. multinomialEntropy_n1_eq_source (proved): H(Multinomial(1,p)) = -∑ pᵢ log pᵢ.
sections.mathContext: At $n=1$, each composition is an indicator function $\delta_j$ for some $j \in s$. The multinomial coefficient $\text{multinomial}(s, \delta_j) = 1$ and $\prod p_i^{\delta_j(i)} = p_j$. So $H = -\sum_j p_j \log p_j = H(p)$.

sections.title: Entropy Upper Bound
sections.summary: multinomialEntropy_upper_bound (proved): H(X) ≤ log|Comp(s,n)| with equality for uniform input.
sections.mathContext: By Gibbs inequality applied to uniform Q on Comp(s,n): $H(P) \leq -\sum_k P(k)\log(1/|\text{Comp}|) = \log|\text{Comp}|$.

sections.title: Binomial Case
sections.summary: For s = {false, true} with p(true) = p, p(false) = 1-p, the multinomial entropy is nonneg.

crossReferences.description: Answers OQ-02: Can multinomial entropy be formalized?
Shannon entropy definition and non-negativity — same conceptual content for general discrete distributions
Markov bound for birthday problem also uses multinomial probability structure

conclusion.summary: YES, the Shannon entropy of the multinomial distribution can be fully formalized in Lean 4 with 0 axioms and 0 sorries. Non-negativity, zero-trial determinism, source entropy recovery at n=1, and the Gibbs upper bound are all machine-checked.
conclusion.implications: The formalization provides a foundation for information-theoretic reasoning about multinomial experiments: entropy bounds for hypothesis testing, channel capacity for categorical channels, and the maximum entropy principle for categorical distributions.
openQuestions: Can the bijection piAntidiag s 1 ≃ s be expressed cleanly using Finset.sum_nbij or Finset.equiv_of_eq?
Can the multinomial CLT be stated: (Xᵢ - npᵢ)/√(npᵢ(1-pᵢ)) → N(0,1) in distribution?
Can the maximum entropy property be proved: the uniform input maximizes H(X) among all p with ∑ pᵢ = 1?
